note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. `hasCriticalFinding` covers only perforation/leak and obstruction — a fistula grades major severity via its own dedicated rule but is deliberately not in that predicate, so it escalates to 'urgent' follow-up, not 'critical-alert'.

personas.name: normal-barium-swallow-complete
personas.description: A normal barium swallow for intermittent dysphagia: normal peristalsis, no stricture, filling defect, reflux, fistula, or obstruction, every mandatory report section present — expect normal classification + none severity + 100% completeness + routine follow-up + no-action.

state.clinicalHistory: Intermittent dysphagia to solids; barium swallow to assess oesophageal motility and structure.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: No previous barium swallow available for comparison.
state.findingsNarrative: Normal oesophageal peristalsis throughout. No stricture, filling defect, reflux, fistula, or obstruction. Smooth mucosal outline.
state.impression: Normal barium swallow; no structural or motility abnormality identified.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No further fluoroscopic follow-up required for this indication.

expected.recommendedAction: No specific imaging follow-up required; manage per usual care.

firedRules.description: No abnormal structured findings on an interpretable examination; classified as normal.
No abnormal finding; abnormality severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: abnormal-enterocutaneous-fistula-major-not-critical-complete
personas.description: A barium follow-through for known Crohn's disease demonstrates a fistulous tract between the terminal ileum and the skin of the right iliac fossa: the fistula grades major severity via its own dedicated rule, but a fistula is deliberately not one of the two triggers in `hasCriticalFinding` (perforation/leak, obstruction), so it escalates only to 'urgent' follow-up, not 'critical-alert'; report complete — expect abnormal classification + major severity + 100% completeness + urgent follow-up + specialist-referral.

state.clinicalHistory: Known Crohn's disease with persistent perianal discharge; barium follow-through to assess for an enteric fistula.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: Previous follow-through 2 years ago showed terminal ileal Crohn changes without a fistula.
state.findingsNarrative: A fistulous tract is demonstrated between the terminal ileum and the skin of the right iliac fossa, in keeping with an enterocutaneous fistula. No free perforation or obstruction.
state.impression: Enterocutaneous fistula arising from the terminal ileum, in keeping with active Crohn's disease.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Refer to the gastroenterology / colorectal surgical MDT for fistula management.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent clinical review and expedite onward referral.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal structured findings are present; classified as abnormal.
A fistulous tract is demonstrated; abnormality severity graded major.
Major abnormality present; follow-up urgency graded urgent.

flags.description: A fistulous tract requiring timely action is present.
flags.suggestedAction: Ensure the referrer is alerted and a clear action plan is documented.

personas.name: critical-anastomotic-leak-uncommunicated-incomplete
personas.description: A water-soluble contrast swallow shows contrast extravasation at the oesophago-gastric anastomosis, in keeping with an anastomotic leak: this critical finding (perforation / leak) auto-escalates classification to critical and follow-up to critical-alert regardless of the other axes; the result has not yet been recorded as communicated, no originating request is linked, and the clinical history and impression sections are not yet completed while the surgical team responds — expect critical classification + major severity + 40% completeness + critical-alert follow-up + urgent-review.

state.findingsNarrative: Contrast extravasation is seen at the oesophago-gastric anastomosis, in keeping with an anastomotic leak. No contained collection seen on this study.
state.clinicianNotes: Phoned through to the surgical team immediately; patient kept nil by mouth pending review.

expected.recommendedAction: Communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now and document the conversation.
